title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 3)
summary: Third Hagakure session on habits and discipline, patient and compassionate teaching, preparation, determination and modern men's weakness. He links passages to building fitness habits slowly, lifting with intent and repressed aggression in modern society.
claims: Fitness discipline is built over time through habits; you cannot rely on motivation, which is fleeting
Discipline can take years to build but then usually lasts for life, helped by rewards such as endorphins and feeling healthier
Bad habits can form in a weekend and are hard to destroy because they feel good and take no effort, like eating a bag of chips
He is not a personal coach because he is too impatient and too hard on people
Beginners burn out by going too fast: jumping from junk food to dry chicken and broccoli lasts two weeks, and training three hours a day without work capacity makes you miserable
Being consistent for a full year beats being obsessed for two weeks
Humiliating people does not make them better; teachers need compassion, empathy and patience, especially with resistant people
Older-generation coaches motivated him by calling him a wimp; he still tends to do this and it is never well received
He does not subscribe to the bushido custom of taking blame to protect a superior's face
Understanding one thing deeply helps you understand ten thousand things, as with related languages, though some learners get confused by them instead
Prepare for realistic scenarios but do not waste energy worrying about one-in-a-million events
Like calligraphy done with determination, act decisively; in lifting, even if you lift slowly you must show intent
When something goes wrong, do not throw a pity party; reflect and try again
Rather than obeying a master, obey your own path; if you do not walk your path you are walking someone else's
His channel's audience is 98 percent men
As a kid he was targeted by bullies who sensed his weakness; once he started working out it stopped, even in a dangerous area
Because most people are weak and do not take care of themselves, lifting and self-respect alone put you in the top 1 percent
Scars should be earned; self-inflicted ones are not manly
Society's taboo on violence hides aggression that turns into frustration and eventually severe violence; passive aggression is worse than open confrontation
More physical activity in schools would teach young people to control their emotions
Most of YouTube fitness is now drama and back-talk, negativity that goes nowhere
Conflicts settled with fists release the pressure and can even end in friendship
